results.title: session.status event should include parentID to distinguish subagent sessions · Issue #30043 · anomalyco/opencode · GitHub
excerpts:
# session.status event should include parentID to distinguish subagent sessions

- Page: GitHub issue
- URL: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/30043
- State: closed (completed)
- Author: aqeelat
- Created: 2026-05-31T02:41:49Z
- Updated: 2026-05-31T16:09:13Z
- Repository: anomalyco/opencode
- Number: #30043
- Comments: 1
- Assignees: nexxeln

---

## Problem

When opencode spawns a subagent (via the Task tool), the subagent runs as a **child session** with its own lifecycle. When the subagent completes, it emits a `session.status` idle event that is structurally identical to the one emitted when the **main session** completes:

```json
{"id":"evt_xxx","type":"session.status","properties":{"sessionID":"ses_child123","status":{"type":"idle"}}}
```

Consumers watching the SSE event stream (e.g. the Warp terminal plugin `@warp-dot-dev/opencode-warp`) see this idle event and mark the tab as "done", even though the main agent session is still running.
The `parentID` field exists on the session model (`session.info.parentID`) and is populated when subagents are created in `tool/task.ts`, but it is **not included** in the `session.status` event — only in `session.created` and `session.updated`.

## Proposed Fix

Add an optional `parentID` field to the `session.status` event schema so consumers can immediately distinguish subagent idle events from main session idle events, without needing to track `session.created` events separately.

### Patch

`packages/opencode/src/session/status.ts`:

```diff
 export const Event = {
   Status: BusEvent.define(
     "session.status",
     Schema.Struct({
       sessionID: SessionID,
       status: Info,
+      parentID: Schema.optional(SessionID),
     }),
   ),
   // deprecated
   Idle: BusEvent.define(
     "session.idle",
     Schema.Struct({
       sessionID: SessionID,
     }),
   ),
 }
```

Then in `SessionStatus.set`, the `parentID` needs to be resolved and passed through.
The session info (including `parentID`) can be fetched from the `Session` service at publish time, or passed as an additional parameter.

This is backward compatible — the field is optional and existing consumers that ignore it will continue to work.

## Consumer Guidance

After this ships, consumers watching for session completion should filter:

```typescript
// Only react to main session completion
if (event.type === "session.status" && event.properties.status.type === "idle") {
  if (event.properties.parentID) return // subagent — ignore
  // main session is done
}
```

results.title: [Bug] Task tool loses session ID (task_id) when sub-agent fails or is cancelled — primary agent cannot recover · Issue #13910 · anomalyco/opencode · GitHub

# [Bug] Task tool loses session ID (task_id) when sub-agent fails or is cancelled — primary agent cannot recover

- Page: GitHub issue
- URL: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/13910
- State: closed (completed)
- Author: diegonix
- Created: 2026-02-17T00:04:18Z
- Updated: 2026-04-19T03:03:50Z
- Repository: anomalyco/opencode
- Number: #13910
- Comments: 5
- Assignees: rekram1-node

## Labels

- bug

---

### Description

When the primary agent dispatches work to a sub-agent via the task tool, the sub-agent's `session.id (task_id)` is only returned on the success path. If the sub-agent crashes, times out, or is cancelled by the user, `SessionPrompt.prompt()` throws and the `task_id` is never communicated back to the calling agent.

This makes recovery impossible: the primary agent has no "handle" to reuse or inspect the failed sub-agent session.

## Root Cause

In `packages/opencode/src/tool/task.ts (≈ lines 128–162)`:
```
// No try-catch around this call:
const result = await SessionPrompt.prompt({
  sessionID: session.id,
  // ...
})

// task_id is only included in the SUCCESSFUL return:
const output = [
  `task_id: ${session.id} (for resuming to continue this task if needed)`,
  "",
  "<task_result>",
  text,
  "</task_result>",
].join("\n")

return { title: params.description, metadata: { sessionId: session.id, model }, output }
```

If `SessionPrompt.prompt()` throws (cancellation, timeout, LLM error, etc.), the exception propagates without any `session.id` context. The primary agent receives a generic "Tool execution aborted" error with no way to reference or resume the sub-session.

## Impact

No recovery: The LLM cannot call `task` with reuse: `<task_id>` because it never received the ID.
Wasted work & cost: All tokens/actions from the failed sub-agent are invisible and unreachable.

...

x (also affects 1.0.x and 1.1.x)
Affects all providers and models

## Related Issues

#9003 — main agent hangs because of subagent (explore)
#6573 — Sessions hang indefinitely when Task tool spawns subagents via REST API

### Plugins

_No response_

### OpenCode version

1.2.0

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open a session with any model (e.g. Claude Opus 4.6) and send a prompt complex enough to trigger the task tool (e.g. "Explore the codebase and explain how authentication works").
2. While the sub-agent is running, press Esc to cancel execution (or wait for it to hit a timeout / LLM error).
3. Observe that the primary agent receives "Tool execution aborted" with no `task_id` in the response.
4. Ask the primary agent to retry or resume the sub-agent's work — it will acknowledge that it has no session handle to reuse:

`"Eu não reutilizei a sessão anterior porque a tentativa terminou com Tool execution aborted e não retornou task_id. Sem task_id, o contrato me impede de reusar."`

```typescript
results.title: [FEATURE]: Real-time Agent-to-Agent (A2A) & Non-blocking SubAgent Communication · Issue #17303 · anomalyco/opencode · GitHub
excerpts:
- **Limited orchestration**: Complex multi-agent workflows difficult to coordinate

### Proposed Enhancement
Enable real-time, asynchronous Agent-to-Agent (A2A) communication:

**Core Features:**
- SubAgent can send intermediate results/status updates to parent Agent (streaming)
- Parent Agent remains responsive—processes new inputs without blocking on SubAgent
- Non-blocking task execution model (fire-and-forget with callback/listener pattern)
- Optional bi-directional messaging during task lifetime
- Parent Agent can cancel, preempt, or modify SubAgent tasks based on new information

### Use Cases
1. **Complex Workflow Orchestration**: Coordinate multiple SubAgents concurrently with dynamic task management
2. **Real-time Progress Updates**: Stream intermediate results/status to user UI without waiting for full completion
3. **Dynamic Task Adaptation**: Parent Agent responds to user input or errors while SubAgent is still executing
4.
**Agent Negotiation**: SubAgents can request clarification or escalate decisions back to parent
5. **Resource Management**: Parent Agent monitors SubAgent resource usage and can preempt if needed

### Benefits
- **Improved UX**: Agents always responsive; users see real-time progress instead of blocking
- **Better Observability**: Streaming logs/status from SubAgents visible throughout execution
- **Advanced Orchestration**: Enables agent collaboration, negotiation, and adaptive workflows
- **Backward Compatible**: Old synchronous mode remains available for simple workflows

### Implementation Approach
1. **Messaging Layer**: Event-based channel or pub-sub system between parent/child sessions
2. **Async Await Pattern**: Replace blocking `await taskTool.execute()` with non-blocking handlers
3. **Stream-based Results**: Use existing session event streams to deliver intermediate messages
4. **API Design**: Provide both callback-style and promise-style interfaces for flexibility
5.
**Session Linking**: Leverage existing `parentID` in session creation for parent-child relationship

### Technical Considerations
- WebSocket or SSE for real-time delivery (already used in ACP)
- Maintain session isolation while allowing controlled message passing
- Handle error propagation and task cancellation across agent boundaries
- Ensure permission/security model accounts for A2A communication

### Related Issues
- #SubAgent-async
- #A2A-agent-interaction
- Task tool in `packages/opencode/src/tool/task.ts`
- Session management in `packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts`

excerpts:
|-----------|---------|
| `SubagentDefinition` | Core interface representing a subagent with name, description, kind, and reference |
| `SubagentReference` | Record holding URI, kind, and metadata for locating a subagent definition |
| `SubagentResolver` | Strategy for resolving `SubagentReference` → `SubagentDefinition` |
| `SubagentExecutor` | Strategy for executing a `TaskCall` against a `SubagentDefinition` |
| `SubagentType` | Record bundling a `SubagentResolver` and `SubagentExecutor` together for a specific kind |
| `TaskCall` | Input record describing the task to execute (prompt, subagent type, model, etc.) |

### Main Components

1. **TaskTool** - Launches and manages sub-agents using pluggable resolvers and executors
2. **TaskOutputTool** - Retrieves results from background sub-agents
3. **ClaudeSubagentType** - Convenience builder for configuring the Claude subagent type with tools, skills, and model routing

## Built-in Sub-Agents

...

---
name: Bash
description: Command execution specialist for running bash commands. Use this for git operations, command execution, and other terminal tasks.
---
```

**Capabilities:**
- Git operations (commits, branches, merges, status checks)
- Build and test commands (npm, cargo, make, pytest)
- Package management operations
- System operations and environment setup
- DevOps tasks (Docker, deployment scripts)

**Guidelines:**
- Follows git safety protocols (no force push to main, no destructive commands without confirmation)
- Limited to Bash tool only - file reading/editing handled by parent agent

## Quick Start

### Basic Setup (Claude subagents only)

```java
import org.springaicommunity.agent.tools.task.TaskTool;
import org.springaicommunity.agent.tools.task.claude.ClaudeSubagentType;

@Configuration
public class AgentConfig {

    @Bean
    CommandLineRunner demo(ChatClient.Builder chatClientBuilder) {
        return args -> {
// Configure Task tool with Claude subagents
            var taskTool = TaskTool.builder()
                .subagentTypes(ClaudeSubagentType.builder()
                    .chatClientBuilder("default", chatClientBuilder)
                    .build())
                .build();

            // Build main chat client with Task tool
            ChatClient chatClient = chatClientBuilder
                .defaultToolCallbacks(taskTool)
                .build();

            // Use naturally - agent will delegate to sub-agents
            String response = chatClient
                .prompt("Explore the authentication module and explain how it works")
                .call()
                .content();
        };
    }
}
```

## Configuration

### Using ClaudeSubagentType

...

- **`model`** — Uses the default provider with the specified model. Short aliases (`opus`, `haiku`, `sonnet`) are mapped to their full Claude model identifiers. The model can also be the full model name of any provider (e.g., `gpt-4o`).
- **`provider:model`** — Uses the named provider with the specified model (e.g., `openai:gpt-4o`, `ollama:llama3`).

If the specified provider is not found in the builder map, or if no model is specified, the default builder is used as a fallback.

### Loading Subagent References

#### From Directories

```java
import org.springaicommunity.agent.tools.task.claude.ClaudeSubagentReferences;

List<SubagentReference> refs = ClaudeSubagentReferences.fromRootDirectory("/path/to/agents");
```

#### From Spring Resources

```java
@Value("${agent.tasks.paths}")
List<Resource> agentPaths;

List<SubagentReference> refs = ClaudeSubagentReferences.fromResources(agentPaths);
```

#### Multiple Sources

```java
List<SubagentReference> refs = ClaudeSubagentReferences.

...

You are a [role description]. You specialize in [domain].

**Your Primary Responsibilities:**
1. [Responsibility 1]
2. [Responsibility 2]

**Guidelines:**
- [Guideline 1]
- [Guideline 2]
```

### Configuration Fields

| Field | Required | Description |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| `name` | Yes | Unique identifier (lowercase with hyphens) |
| `description` | Yes | Natural language purpose description with usage examples |
| `tools` | No | Comma-separated list of allowed tool names (inherits all if omitted) |
| `disallowedTools` | No | Comma-separated list of tools to explicitly deny |
| `model` | No | Model specification: a short alias (`sonnet`, `opus`, `haiku`), a full model name (`gpt-4o`), or `provider:model` (`openai:gpt-4o`) |
| `skills` | No | Comma-separated list of skill names to preload into the subagent's system prompt |
| `permissionMode` | No | Permission handling mode (default: `default`) |

# Native OpenCode subagent panes via session bridge

- Page: GitHub issue
- URL: https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/issues/2479
- State: open
- Author: lawrencecchen
- Created: 2026-04-01T10:05:30Z
- Updated: 2026-04-01T23:06:02Z
- Repository: manaflow-ai/cmux
- Number: #2479
- Assignees: lawrencecchen
- Linked PRs: #2517 (open)

---

OpenCode already has first class child sessions. cmux should support them directly. The lowest risk first step is a hook driven plugin MVP, then a native cmux session bridge if the workflow proves out.

## Why this is feasible

- OpenCode includes a built in `general` subagent and documents subagent use in the main README: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/1df5ad470a49163ad623460b4e969da1b51cc404/README.md
- The task tool creates real child sessions with `parentID: ctx.sessionID`, so subagents are session graph nodes, not just visual panes: https://github.
com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/1df5ad470a49163ad623460b4e969da1b51cc404/packages/opencode/src/tool/task.ts
- Upstream already exposes an attach primitive for an existing session. `opencode attach <url>` accepts `--session <id>`: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/1df5ad470a49163ad623460b4e969da1b51cc404/packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/tui/attach.ts
- The server API exposes `GET /session/:id/children` and an SSE `/event` stream, which is enough to discover and backfill child session state: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/1df5ad470a49163ad623460b4e969da1b51cc404/packages/web/src/content/docs/server.mdx and https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/1df5ad470a49163ad623460b4e969da1b51cc404/packages/web/src/content/docs/server.mdx
- Plugins can subscribe to `session.created`, `session.deleted`, `session.status`, and `session.updated`, and plugin code gets Bun's `$` shell API plus OpenCode context: https://github.

results.title: Web UI session list shows subagent and archived sessions that TUI hides · Issue #14053 · anomalyco/opencode · GitHub

# Web UI session list shows subagent and archived sessions that TUI hides

- Page: GitHub issue
- URL: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/14053
- State: closed (completed)
- Author: lauwah
- Created: 2026-02-18T00:42:24Z
- Updated: 2026-04-19T03:04:08Z
- Repository: anomalyco/opencode
- Number: #14053
- Comments: 1
- Assignees: rekram1-node

## Labels

- bug
- core

---

### Description

The Web UI (`opencode serve`) shows **all** sessions including subagent (child) sessions and archived sessions in the session list, while the TUI (`opencode session list`) correctly filters these out. This causes confusion as users see different session counts between the two interfaces.

Subagent sessions are created internally by the Task tool and have a `parentID` field. Archived sessions have `time.archived` set. Both should be hidden from the user-facing session list in the Web UI, matching the TUI behavior.
Example from the `/session` API response — these sessions have `parentID` and should be hidden:

```json
{"id": "ses_39525b99...", "parentID": "ses_39608f5b...", "title": "Research Claude Code iPhone (@general subagent)"}
{"id": "ses_3a0ab433...", "parentID": "ses_3a0abdf1...", "title": "Investigate Discord agent mobile issue (@explore subagent)"}
```

### Plugins

None

### OpenCode version

0.0.0-dev-202602110224

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start opencode serve --port 4096
2. 2. In TUI or any session, use the Task tool (which creates subagent sessions with parentID)
3. 3. Compare session lists:
4.    - TUI (opencode session list): Shows only top-level, non-archived sessions (e.g. 9 sessions)
5.    - Web UI session sidebar: Shows all sessions including subagent children (e.g. 11 sessions)
6. 4. The Web UI count is always higher because it includes subagent and archived sessions

### Screenshot and/or share link

_No response_

### Operating System

macOS (darwin, arm64)
